quotes.text: The Accounts v2 API is generally available for Connect users, and in public preview for other Stripe users. If you’re part of the Accounts v2 preview, you need to specify a [preview version](https://docs.stripe.com/api-v2-overview.md#sdk-and-api-versioning) in your code.

For most use cases, we recommend [modeling your customers as customer-configured Account objects](https://docs.stripe.com/accounts-v2/use-accounts-as-customers.md) instead of using [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers.md) objects.

Checkout redirects your customer to the `success_url` when you [acknowledge you received the event](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks.md#acknowledge-events-immediately). In scenarios where your endpoint is down or the event isn’t acknowledged properly, Checkout redirects the customer to the `success_url` 10 seconds after a successful payment.

findings: The new capture is a 765-line full iOS app-to-web Checkout guide, not a navigation index. The US iOS digital-goods scope and StoreKit storefront test remain (old:10-18; new:13-21); Android US direct in-app processing is a separate route, and Managed Payments is an optional merchant-of-record guide (old:8,12,555-557; new:9,15,751-753). A captured statement does not establish current regional eligibility or App Store approval.

New raw:26,30-36 adds a customer-configured Accounts v2 path, explicitly generally available for Connect users but public preview for other Stripe users, with preview-version and Dashboard preview instructions for preview participants. It recommends Accounts for most use cases; Customers v1 remains a full branch at new:227-256,419-524. Old raw:22-25,143-172,228-332 only modeled Customer v1. Current source:13,27-28,54-65,82-88 implies Customer-only; update those sections with separate qualified v2/v1 identities and examples, not a universal replacement.

Accounts v2 examples create stripe.v2.core.accounts at new:198-219 and pass customer_account in one-time and subscription Checkout Sessions at new:345-358,391-404. The older Customers v1 examples still pass customer at new:451-464,498-511. New integration_identifier appears in both paths as an integration label/conversion-measurement example (new:356-357,402-403,462-463,509-510); it is not evidence of a required field or realized conversion tracking.

New raw:11 adds Checkout studio configure/preview navigation, and new:755-757 adds optional yearly-subscription monthly-term and tax display settings. Neither changes the US iOS eligibility premise. The old/new Universal Links, Safari, StoreKit gate, and checkout.session.completed fulfillment instructions persist (old:174-226,334-378,427-431; new:258-310,526-570,620-624).

Current source:27-32 lists Checkout redirect at step 5 before server receipt and entitlement grant at step 6, while both captures explain Checkout waits for webhook acknowledgement before redirect or falls back to redirect after 10 seconds if not acknowledged (old:429-431; new:620-624). Replace the strict sequence with webhook-led fulfillment and a separately timed return; a success URL is not fulfillment proof.

Current source Swift excerpt at source:69-80 sets paymentComplete from a success URL substring and omits the source guide's instruction to fetch latest customer entitlements from the server (old:365-371; new:557-563). Preserve the sample as illustrative UI handling only and explicitly route authoritative purchase/credit state through server webhook/entitlement data. The raw sample's own webhook lookup uses session.customer at new:666-673 even though the new Accounts v2 Session path supplies customer_account; this internal example mismatch should be noted for follow-up rather than presented as verified v2 fulfillment behavior.
substantive_changes: Adds qualified Accounts v2 customer identity and Checkout Session customer_account examples while retaining Customer v1, including Connect GA versus other-user public preview and preview version qualification (new:26,30-36,194-256,312-524; old:22-25,143-172,228-332).

Adds integration_identifier as a labeled conversion-segmentation example in both one-time and subscription Session snippets (new:356-357,402-403,462-463,509-510); adds Checkout studio route and optional price display settings (new:11,755-757).

Diff also changes setup sample language from Node npm to Ruby gem and CLI npm instructions (old:49-59; new:74-104), while most later changes are Markdown, code formatting, image URLs, and numbered-list normalization.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the prior US iOS digital-goods app-to-web scope and distinction from Android in-app payments, physical/outside-app goods, and optional Managed Payments (old:8-18; new:9,13-21,751-753).
Keep Customers v1 as a documented path, not a deprecated path inferred from the new v2 recommendation (old:143-172,228-332; new:227-256,419-524).

Keep Universal Link association, fallback page, Safari opening, StoreKit canMakePayments gate, and webhook-backed coin grant as separate steps (old:174-226,334-378,427-431; new:258-310,526-570,620-624).
conflicts: Source:13,27-28,54-65,82-88 presents the Checkout identity/fulfillment path as Customer-only. New raw:30-36,194-256,312-524 documents qualified customer-configured Accounts v2 alongside retained Customers v1. Source and any one-line concept route should distinguish the two branches and the preview gate; do not replace v1 wholesale.

Source:27-32 sequences redirect before webhook entitlement grant, but old:429-431 and new:620-624 state redirect on webhook acknowledgement with a 10-second fallback after successful payment. Source:69-80 also promotes a URL substring to paymentComplete without including the raw's server entitlement refresh comment (old:365-371; new:557-563). Correct both so client redirect is not treated as finality and entitlement is server-owned.

The new Accounts v2 Session examples use customer_account (new:354,400), while the shared webhook sample still indexes session.customer (new:666-673). This capture does not demonstrate a working v2 account-to-user lookup; mark the sample mismatch and avoid claiming v2 webhook fulfillment has been verified.
unresolved_questions: The four pinned files do not resolve whether the shared webhook example's session.customer lookup works for a customer_account Session, or how account-based entitlement lookup should be implemented. Confirm from an independently pinned API source before documenting that mapping.
The capture documents dated US iOS storefront and Accounts v2 availability/preview wording; live App Store policy, account eligibility, and runtime behavior were not checked in this review.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/mobile/digital-goods/checkout, the new capture is still a complete iOS US digital-goods app-to-web Checkout guide (new raw:5-28; old raw:4-25), but adds customer-configured Accounts v2 as a second identity path (new:30-36,194-256,312-418). Accounts v2 is GA for Connect users and public preview for others, with a preview version required for preview participants; Customers v1 remains documented at new:227-256,419-524. [[source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-checkout]] needs the qualified split because its summary and code currently describe only Customer v1 (source:13,27-28,54-65).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/mobile/digital-goods/checkout, update [[source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-checkout]] for the new Accounts v2/customer_account and retained Customers v1/customer alternatives (new raw:30-36,194-256,312-524; old raw:143-172,228-332), without implying v1 deprecation or broad availability. Repair existing source:27-32 redirect-before-webhook order and source:69-80 URL-substring paymentComplete example: both captures require webhook-led server credit and say Checkout waits for acknowledgement or uses a 10-second redirect fallback (old:427-431; new:620-624), while the sample calls for refreshed server entitlements (old:365-371; new:557-563). Flag the new v2 customer_account versus shared webhook session.customer mismatch (new:354,666-673) as unresolved, and keep concept routes to this source qualified rather than copying unverified fulfillment behavior.
